Plot an interpretation

Source: R/verb-interpret.R
plot.survalis_interpret.Rd

Draws the result of interpret() with the plot of its method. Plots have no title unless title is given, and return a ggplot to which layers can be added.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'survalis_interpret'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A survalis_interpret object.

...

Passed to the method's plot. Useful ones:

  • title (all methods; subtitle and caption too for "roc" and "dca").

  • time.labels ("pdp", "ice", "ale"): labels of the time panels or legend. NULL gives "t = 365", a string is the unit ("days" gives "t = 365 days"), and a function maps the times to labels, for example function(t) paste(t / 365, "years").

  • colors: "pdp" / "ice" the ICE and PDP colours (default grey and blue); "roc" the curve colour; "dca" the model, treat-all and treat-none colours. Colours are set through the theme palette (ggplot2 >= 4.0), so a scale_colour_manual() added afterwards also works, without a message; a complete theme added afterwards (e.g. theme_bw()) resets them, so prefer colors then.

  • auc ("roc"): print the AUC in the panel (default TRUE).

Value

A ggplot.

Examples

m <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, veteran, "coxph")
plot(interpret(m, "pdp", feature = "karno", times = c(90, 180)),
     time.labels = "days")

plot(interpret(m, "dca", eval_time = 180), colors = c("black", "grey50", "grey80"))
